topic.title: A $4,500 Video Built Dollar Shave Club

title: One $4,500 Video Built Dollar Shave Club
description:
How did one cheap video turn Dollar Shave Club into a company Unilever reportedly bought?
Dollar Shave Club, 2012 to 2016, told from its founder's interview and the deal reports.
Sources: Fortune (Jul 2016).
Based on public records and reporting. Not financial or legal advice.

lines.text: Dollar Shave Club started with one video that cost about $4,500.
The day it went up, investors put in $1M. Then the orders poured in.
Its bet: razor blades mailed to your door every month, instead of a trip to the shop. Would anyone sign up?
The founder told Fortune it sold $4M in its first year, $19M the next, then $65M.
So what is a box of mailed razors really worth?
Four years after that video, Unilever, the company behind Dove soap, came to buy it.
Fortune's sources put the price at $1B, all in cash, for a company one cheap video started.
Mailed blades or the shop shelf: where do you buy yours? Either way, it all goes back to one video.

All 6 facts confirmed on the Fortune pages (WebFetch): Dubin interview 10 Mar 2015 states video ~$4,500, $1M seed closed 6 Mar 2012 same day as launch, revenue $4M/$19M/$65M for 2012/13/14 (attributed to the founder in voice and on screen); Fortune 19 Jul 2016 reports $1B in cash from sources close to the deal, terms undisclosed (voice says 'Fortune's sources', screen says 'reported, price not disclosed'). Verify list met; no advice, disclaimer ends description.
